sections.section_title: Focused background: TAVI durability, redo-TAVI, and post-endocarditis considerations
sections.description: Concise concepts needed to understand why a third transcatheter aortic valve was contemplated and how prior infection affects planning.
subtopics: Evolution of TAVI indications and the rising need for reinterventions as longevity increases
Mechanisms of transcatheter structural valve deterioration (leaflet fibrosis/calcification, frame underexpansion) and timelines
Prosthesis–patient mismatch (PPM): definitions (indexed EOA, Doppler velocity index), clinical impact, and why PPM risk escalates with serial TAVR
Hazards unique to TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV: coronary obstruction, reduced effective orifice area, impaired coronary reaccess, frame layering

Key points from 2025 ESC guidance: surgery preferred for active/complicated PVE; prerequisites before any transcatheter redo (infection control, negative cultures, imaging clearance, individualized heart-team decision)

Device design features pertinent to this case: mechanically expanded Lotus vs self-expanding Evolut vs self-expanding Acurate neo2 (supra-annular leaflet position, frame height, commissural alignment capability) and implications for frame interaction

sections.section_title: Case chronology, presentation, and diagnostic synthesis
sections.description: Timeline from initial TAVI to current presentation, key comorbidities, and how multimodality data established the problem list and severity.
subtopics: Baseline risk profile: hypertension, 3-vessel CAD with multiple PCIs, AV block with pacemaker, COPD, diabetes, recurrent GI bleeding
Prior valve history: 27 mm Lotus (2014) for severe AS; symptomatic degeneration leading to 23 mm Evolut TAV-in-TAV (2022) complicated by femoral pseudoaneurysm
Prosthetic valve endocarditis (2022): Enterococcus faecalis, targeted 6-week IV therapy then oral per ID, subsequent clinical and imaging resolution
Current symptoms and functional limitation prompting re-evaluation (2024): exertional dyspnoea, chest spasm, dizziness, fatigue

Echocardiography at key stages: EF drop to 42% pre-2022 redo then recovery to 54% post-2022; by 2024 severe stenosis with moderate–severe regurgitation, mean gradient 49 mm Hg, AVA 0.5 cm²; DVI 0.24 at post-implant evaluation
TEE and CT to exclude active endocarditis before third TAVI; repeated negative blood cultures
CT anatomy relevant to feasibility: minimum lumen 13.7 mm within Evolut frame; two overlapping frames visualised
Surgical ineligibility synthesis: EuroSCORE II 27.36%, extensive comorbidity, and deeply integrated stented frames implying high-risk, technically hazardous explant/root replacement
Clinical problem statement: severe prosthetic dysfunction (stenosis with regurgitation) in double-stented valve after treated PVE with prohibitive surgical risk

sections.section_title: CT-guided planning for a third TAVI: goals, measurements, and strategy
sections.description: How imaging translated into a procedural plan that balanced haemodynamics, coronary safety, and future coronary access in a triple-stented anatomy.
subtopics: Planning goals: preserve coronary flow and future access; maximise effective orifice area; mitigate PPM; ensure commissural alignment; minimise procedural risk

MSCT measurements and analyses: coronary ostial heights; sinus of Valsalva and sinotubular junction dimensions; valve-to-coronary distances; anticipated neo-skirt height and leaflet-to-ostium relationships; internal dimensions across prior frames
Frame interaction mapping: identifying Evolut commissures/leaflets; selecting a high implant depth to pin prior leaflets, limit inward leaflet folding, and keep the neo-skirt below the coronary ostia
Valve selection and sizing: rationale for Acurate neo2 (size S) with supra-annular leaflets, relatively low frame, and alignment features suited to narrow landing zones
Coronary protection decision: criteria supporting avoidance (adequate CT-derived clearances) while preparing bailouts (chimney stenting, BASILICA) if needed

PPM mitigation plan: pre-dilation to assess expandability and gradients; commissural alignment to optimise central flow; readiness for post-dilation to enhance prior frame expansion without intentional fracture

sections.section_title: Procedural execution and intraprocedural decision points
sections.description: Step-by-step technical conduct of the TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV and real-time checks that ensured coronary safety and haemodynamic optimisation.
subtopics: Access and monitoring: local anaesthesia; left radial and left femoral arterial access; haemodynamic support and rapid pacing setup
Baseline aortography confirming severe aortic regurgitation; LV wiring with a Safari guidewire
Balloon pre-dilation (22×40 mm) under rapid pacing (≈180 bpm) with simultaneous aortography to verify unobstructed coronary flow
Acurate neo2 (S) deployment: aligning to Evolut leaflet/commissural landmarks based on preprocedural CT; deliberate high implantation strategy
Post-dilation (20×40 mm) to optimise expansion and leaflet motion; angiographic endpoints: valve position, absence of paravalvular/transvalvular leak, preserved coronary perfusion
Bailout preparedness and resource planning: equipment availability, radiation/contrast management in complex redo cases

sections.section_title: Outcomes, haemodynamic interpretation, and longitudinal surveillance
sections.description: Immediate and follow-up results, why gradients evolved over time, and how to structure ongoing monitoring after a triple-stented aortic valve.
subtopics: Immediate post-implant per VARC-3: correct position, no regurgitation, but high mean gradient 67 mm Hg; AVA 0.9 cm² (indexed 0.4 cm²/m²); DVI 0.24 consistent with severe PPM
Physiological interpretation of early high gradients: leaflet pinning dynamics, partial mechanical expansion of prior frame with post-dilation, recovery of LV stroke volume, improved central flow
Serial echocardiography: 1 month mean gradient 27 mm Hg, AVA 1.1 cm²; 3.5 months asymptomatic with stable haemodynamics; 1 year mean gradient 26 mm Hg, AVA 1.1 cm², EF ~65%, no regurgitation
Clinical course: asymptomatic status, no heart failure or recurrent infection; durability signal at 1 year in a triple-stented configuration
Surveillance framework: timing of TTE, triggers for CT, vigilance for PVE recurrence, coronary access planning if future PCI is required, thresholds for considering reintervention

sections.section_title: Clinical lessons, decision frameworks, and future directions
sections.description: Actionable takeaways for trainees and teams facing serial transcatheter valve failures, particularly after treated PVE.
subtopics: Heart-team checklist for TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV after PVE: infection control and documentation; comprehensive CT planning; echo haemodynamics; surgical risk quantification; shared decision-making and informed consent (including off-label use)
Selecting transcatheter vs surgical redo: recognizing when deep, integrated frames imply the need for root/ascending aorta replacement and prohibitive risk
Lifetime management starting at index TAVI: anticipate reinterventions, prioritise commissural alignment and coronary reaccess, and choose devices with future trajectories in mind
Coronary safety strategies in serial TAVR: high implant, commissural alignment, device/frame selection; when to use BASILICA or chimney stenting
PPM awareness and mitigation in redo TAVR: preprocedural prediction, intra-procedural optimisation, and interpretation of indexed AVA and DVI post-implant
Evidence gaps and research needs: long-term outcomes of triple-stented valves, advanced 3D modelling for frame expansion prediction, and guidance on endocarditis risk after serial TAVR
